Exports grew +12% YoY 2025 (HIGH). Retail forecast CAGRs are 5.9-6.2% (LOW). Production, export, and retail growth measure different things and should be read separately. The strongest figure is production (MEDIUM), which is factory-gate output — inflated by Korea's export-manufacturing role, not a home-demand read; the two retail estimates are LOW and modestly conflicting; exports are a separate EXPORT_FOB measure.

A separate figure puts the mass tier at 79.55% of colour_cosmetics market share for 2025 (RETAIL basis, LOW confidence, Mordor Intelligence), suggesting the segment is currently mass-tier dominated by this estimate. New sub-segment sizings (face_makeup ~US$1.89bn, lip_colour ~US$1.39bn, nail ~US$0.83bn, 2024, MRFF LOW) now give a rough internal breakdown. No whole-segment growth_yoy figure is present for India colour_cosmetics. The market-size note references a forecast CAGR of ~7.08%, and a lipstick-only sub read shows ~9.6% CAGR (TechSci/Markets and Data) — both forward-looking forecasts, not observed growth. India figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates; the segment total and the sub-segment splits come from different houses on different definitions, so the parts will not sum cleanly to the whole, and organised-vs-unorganised coverage is unstated.

passages.title: Analyst read — colour cosmetics (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional comparison is possible: India (~US$3.46bn, LOW) is larger than Korea's retail colour cosmetics (~US$2.2-2.9bn, LOW), though every figure here is LOW confidence. The sharper contrast is structural — Korea's production (KRW 2.68tn, ~15% of national cosmetics output) reflects its role as a global colour-cosmetics manufacturing hub feeding US$1.51bn of exports, whereas India's number is a home-demand retail estimate. On the corridor, colour cosmetics shows real if unquantified K-beauty pull (Hince via Tira Jan-2026, Etude tints on Blinkit), but no [CORRIDOR]-tagged market figure exists yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's dermocosmetics segment now has a size anchor, but the Korean sources disagree sharply. Samjong KPMG (via Korea Herald) puts the market at KRW 4.5tn in 2020 (MEDIUM, RETAIL); the Korean Enterprise Reputation Research body also cites KRW 4.5tn but for 2022, with KRW 5.5tn projected for 2025; and a cosmeceutical institute gives a much lower KRW 1.2tn for 2020. That is a definitional tangle — 'dermocosmetics/cosmeceutical' is drawn differently by each — so the figure is anchored around the low-single-digit KRW-trillions but not pinned. Euromonitor's HIGH-confidence +13% YoY growth (2024) still stands as the most reliable single datapoint. Euromonitor reports +13% YoY for 2024 (HIGH, RETAIL), driven by actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides) — the segment is growing fast. The KERI series (KRW 4.5tn 2022 to a projected 5.5tn 2025) implies continued growth, but is MEDIUM and definitionally loose; no clean derma-specific CAGR forecast is available. The size figures conflict by up to ~4x depending on how 'dermocosmetics' is scoped, and several are recorded on an NA basis because the source definition was unclear — treat scale as indicative; the growth read (Euromonitor, HIGH) is the firmer signal.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: India dermocosmetics is anchored by P&S Market Research at US$0.28bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW) — but that is a narrow, Rx-adjacent definition (US$256mn 2023 base, ~10.3% CAGR to US$505mn 2030). A much broader competing estimate (MarkWide US$1.85bn 2026, ~11.6% CAGR) is roughly 7x larger, a pure definitional gap. A masstige-tier-only cut (Expert Market Research US$65.55mn 2025, 14.6% CAGR) sits below both. Derma-D2C revenue is now on file too (Minimalist Rs347cr FY24, NET_REALISATION). All reads point to fast growth — forecast CAGRs span ~10% (P&S, narrow) to ~15% (EMR, masstige) — but every one is a LOW-confidence forecast, not observed growth. Minimalist's Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr (FY24) revenue jump is a single-company signal, not the segment's rate. The ~7x spread between the narrow (P&S) and broad (MarkWide) sizings means India dermocosmetics scale is genuinely unresolved in the data; all sources are LOW confidence with differing organised/Rx scope.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry a value_usd_bn size, so a rough comparison is possible — Korea (KRW ~4.5tn ≈ US$3bn, MEDIUM) is an order of magnitude larger than India's narrow US$0.28bn read, and still larger than India's broad US$1.85bn read — but both sides are definitionally unstable (KR sources ~4x apart, IN sources ~7x apart), so this is directional, not a firm ratio. The more decision-relevant fact is momentum plus corridor fit: both markets are growing double-digit, and dermocosmetics is the corridor's highest-conviction whitespace (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3). Fresh corridor evidence — Nykaa's K-beauty GMV +60% YoY (Q3 2025), Medicube/Illiyoon/Aestura launching on Nykaa/Tira through 2026 — confirms the pull, though no India brand-level K-derma revenue is published yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's fragrances segment data consists solely of export figures; no domestic retail or production market-size figure is present. The most recent export value is US$0.06bn (2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH confidence, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald). A separate HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade figure puts 2024 HS 3303 exports to the world at US$0.039471bn - a different source and period than the MFDS total, so the two should not be read as one continuous series. Of that 2024 world-export figure, only US$6,000 (0.000006bn) went to India, a [CORRIDOR]-tagged flow that is a negligible share of Korea's total fragrance exports. The MFDS-sourced 2025 export figure carries a +46.2% observed year-on-year note, off what the source itself calls a small base. No cagr_forecast or domestic-market growth figure is present, so growth direction for the segment beyond exports cannot be assessed from current data. No domestic retail or production market size exists for Korea fragrances in the current data - only export values, and those two export figures differ in source, period, and scope (2025 MFDS total vs. 2024 Comtrade HS3303-to-world), so they should not be combined.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (India)
passages.text: India fragrances has two RETAIL market-size estimates, both LOW confidence: US$2.6bn (2024) covering perfume plus deodorant combined, and a narrower US$0.281bn (FY24) covering perfume only - different scope, so not directly comparable to each other. Import data is HIGH confidence: India imported US$0.331681bn of fragrances (HS 3303) from the world in 2024, with Korea (US$0.000135bn, [CORRIDOR]-tagged) and China (US$0.000249bn) each a minor source. An ESTIMATE-confidence import-dependence figure of 12.8% notes that premium fragrance is import-reliant (UAE the largest source, then France) while mass-market perfume/deodorant is largely made domestically. A MEDIUM-confidence company figure (Vini Cosmetics/Fogg, FY25 revenue INR 1200cr, NET_REALISATION basis) is also present but reflects one company, not the segment as a whole. No top-level growth_yoy or cagr_forecast is populated for India fragrances. The notes on both market-size figures do carry forward-looking CAGRs - roughly 11.1% to US$6.7bn by 2033 for the perfume+deodorant estimate, and 15.23% to US$0.873bn by FY2032 for the perfume-only estimate - but both are forecasts, not observed growth, and both come from LOW-confidence sources. Both India market-size figures are LOW-confidence industry/aggregator estimates covering different scope (perfume+deodorant vs. perfume-only), so neither should be treated as a single definitive segment size; the 12.8% import-dependence figure is itself labelled ESTIMATE/derived rather than a directly sourced number.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (Korea vs India)
passages.text: A like-for-like comparison of Korea and India fragrances is not possible with the data at hand: Korea's only figures are EXPORT_FOB export values (US$0.06bn in 2025, US$0.039471bn for 2024 world HS3303), while India's are RETAIL market-size estimates (US$2.6bn or US$0.281bn depending on scope) plus IMPORT_CIF figures - different value_basis on both sides, and neither carries a shared value_usd_bn field that would permit direct netting. The Korea-to-India corridor trade flow is present but tiny on both sides of the ledger (KR exports to India US$6,000 in 2024; India imports from Korea US$135,000 in 2024, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged), suggesting fragrances is a minor thread of the broader K-beauty corridor relative to categories like skincare.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's hair care now has a domestic size anchor: IMARC puts the market at US$1.8bn for 2025 (RETAIL, LOW confidence), forecast to US$2.4bn by 2034. That sits alongside the existing trade picture — total Korean hair-care exports (HS 3305) of US$0.413bn (EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024), of which US$0.003bn went to India ([CORRIDOR]-tagged). IMARC gives a forecast CAGR of 3.23% (2026-2034, LOW) — a modest forward projection, not observed growth. No observed KR growth_yoy is on file for the domestic market; the reliable observed figures remain on the export side. The domestic size is a single LOW-confidence aggregator estimate; the HIGH-confidence figures are exports (EXPORT_FOB), a different basis that cannot substitute for domestic retail scale.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (India)
passages.text: India's hair-care market is sized at US$4.1bn (RETAIL/MRP-inclusive, LOW, Mordor, 2026), with a 'skinification' shift toward actives and serums. Sub-segment detail is now firmer: shampoo ~US$1.26bn (2025), and scalp_care captured through three conflicting proxy measures (alopecia US$267mn, hair serum US$155mn, hair-growth products US$825mn) that reflect how differently 'scalp care' is scoped. India also imported US$0.199bn of hair-care products from the world (US$0.031bn from China) (IMPORT_CIF, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024). A forecast CAGR of 4.73% (2026-2031, LOW, Mordor) is a projection, not observed growth. The scalp-care/serum sub-space is where the 'skinification' momentum sits, but its size proxies are LOW and definitionally scattered. Segment and sub-segment figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates from different houses on different definitions; the three scalp-care measures are not comparable to each other, and organised/unorganised coverage is unstated.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both markets now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn sizes, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$4.1bn, LOW) is roughly 2x Korea's domestic hair care (~US$1.8bn, LOW), though both are single LOW-confidence estimates. The corridor angle is thin in absolute terms — Korea's hair-care exports to India are just US$0.003bn ([CORRIDOR]), consistent with AmorePacific's Mise En Scène and RYO being recent (2025) Nykaa entrants rather than established sellers — while India separately imports US$0.199bn of hair care from the world (IMPORT_CIF, a different basis, not netted). The shared structural story is 'skinification': actives-led scalp/serum demand is the growth edge in both markets, and the clearest near-term corridor opportunity.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's men's grooming segment now has an anchor: Euromonitor (via Korea Herald) sizes men's cosmetics at KRW 1.16tn (~US$0.78bn) for CY2025, MEDIUM confidence, RETAIL basis, up from KRW 1.09tn in 2022. A separate Future Market Insights estimate puts men's SKINCARE alone at US$1.2bn (2025, LOW) — but that implausibly exceeds the whole men's-cosmetics figure, a clear definitional mismatch, so the two cannot be stacked or compared. The Euromonitor series implies modest growth (KRW 1.09tn 2022 to 1.16tn 2025). FMI forecasts an 11.04% CAGR to 2035 (LOW), but on the men's-skincare-only basket, not the whole segment — so it is not this segment's forecast rate. The one reasonably-solid figure (Euromonitor, MEDIUM) covers 'men's cosmetics'; the LOW FMI figure uses a broader, internally-inconsistent skincare basket that exceeds it, so absolute segment scale is anchored but not precise.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: India men's grooming is the better-evidenced side: Euromonitor sizes it at INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) for 2025, HIGH confidence, RETAIL, growing +9% YoY (also HIGH). IBEF frames the trajectory as INR 20,500cr (2024) to INR 38,300cr (2033), MEDIUM. The men's_skincare sub-segment — corridor whitespace #4 — sizes ~US$1.02bn (Deep Market Insights, LOW). Several LOW aggregator whole-segment estimates cluster US$2.3-2.45bn on differing 'male grooming' baskets. Observed +9% YoY for 2025 (HIGH, Euromonitor). Forecast CAGRs span 5-12% (LOW-MEDIUM) depending on basket; IBEF's 2024-2033 path implies roughly 7%. Men's skincare is repeatedly cited as the fastest-growing slice, consistent with the whitespace read, though the sub-segment growth figures themselves are LOW. Only the Euromonitor size and growth are HIGH confidence; the aggregator estimates vary materially in scope (men's cosmetics vs 'male grooming products' vs razors-inclusive), so they corroborate direction, not a precise number.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$1.94bn, HIGH, 2025) is roughly 2.5x the size of Korea's men's cosmetics (~US$0.78bn, MEDIUM, 2025) in absolute terms and is far better evidenced. The confidence gap matters — India's figure is Euromonitor-HIGH, Korea's is Euromonitor-MEDIUM via press — so treat the ratio as directional. Korea's distinction is intensity, not size: it is the world's highest per-capita men's beauty market, whereas India is the larger absolute opportunity with men's skincare flagged as corridor whitespace. No K-beauty men's-grooming-in-India market figure surfaced in research, so the corridor angle here stays qualitative.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: The only KR data available for oral_care is trade-flow, not domestic market size. Korea's HS 3306 (oral hygiene) exports to the world totalled approximately US$0.079986bn (~$80.0m) FOB in 2024, a HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade figure. Of that, exports specifically to India were about US$0.000251bn (~$251,000) FOB in 2024, also HIGH confidence and [CORRIDOR]-tagged, a very small share of total Korean oral care exports. No domestic retail, production, or wholesale figure for Korean oral care exists in the current data. No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast figure is present for either export series, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data. These are single-year (2024) customs export declarations for HS 3306 only, not a market-size estimate, and the India-bound figure is a small corridor subset of total exports rather than segment-wide activity.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (India)
passages.text: IN oral_care data is likewise trade-flow only. India's HS 3306 imports from the world totalled about US$0.01974bn (~$19.7m) CIF in 2024 (HIGH confidence, UN Comtrade). Imports from Korea were about US$0.000485bn (~$485,000) CIF, [CORRIDOR]-tagged, versus US$0.001595bn (~$1.6m) CIF from China, so Korea is a minor supplier relative to China and to India's total oral care imports. No domestic market-size figure is available for this segment. No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast figure is present for any of the three import series, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data. These are single-year (2024) customs import declarations for HS 3306, not a retail market-size estimate, and carry no organised-vs-unorganised split since they describe trade flow rather than domestic sales.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: No RETAIL, NET_REALISATION, or PRODUCTION size figure (and no shaped value_usd_bn size field) exists for oral_care in either geography, so KR and IN cannot be compared as markets here. The only available figures are trade flows recorded on different value bases, Korea's on EXPORT_FOB and India's on IMPORT_CIF, so per the no-netting rule they are not combined into one number. The two [CORRIDOR]-tagged figures, Korea's ~US$0.000251bn FOB export to India versus India's ~US$0.000485bn CIF import from Korea, describe the same HS 3306 flow from opposite customs sides; the difference between them likely reflects the FOB/CIF basis gap and normal mirror-statistics discrepancy rather than two distinct quantities.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Two distinct measures exist for Korea skincare and should not be summed: a HIGH-confidence domestic retail market size of KRW 7.653tn (~US$5.18bn equivalent, 2025, Euromonitor) and a HIGH-confidence export figure of US$8.54bn (EXPORT_FOB, 2025, ~75% of Korea's total cosmetics exports, MFDS). The export number is larger than the retail number because they measure different things (overseas sales vs. domestic sell-through), not because exports exceed the home market. Separate UN Comtrade HS 3304 data show Korea exported US$8.567bn to the world in 2024 (EXPORT_FOB) but only US$0.0656bn of that went to India [CORRIDOR]; HS 3304 also blends makeup with skincare, so this is not a skincare-only cut. Domestic retail grew a modest 1.0% YoY in 2025 (Euromonitor, RETAIL), while skincare-led exports grew 11.6% YoY in 2025 (MFDS, EXPORT_FOB) - two different bases moving at different speeds. No cagr_forecast is present for either measure. The retail and export figures are both HIGH confidence but sit on different value_basis (RETAIL vs EXPORT_FOB) and must never be netted; the Comtrade HS 3304 figures additionally mix makeup into the skincare total.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (India)
passages.text: India's skincare market is sized at US$9.06bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW confidence, IMARC) - LOW because it is an aggregator estimate rather than a primary source. Two market-share reads of skincare's weight in adjacent baskets diverge structurally rather than contradicting each other: IMARC puts skincare/sun care at 35% of total BPC, while Grand View Research puts skincare at 49% of a narrower "cosmetics" basket - different denominators, not comparable directly. HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade data show India importing US$0.844bn of HS 3304 goods (skincare plus makeup) from the world in 2024, of which US$0.140bn came from Korea specifically [CORRIDOR] and US$0.188bn from China; a separate ESTIMATE (not a primary figure, methodology shown) derives import dependence at 9.3%, implying roughly 91% of the market by value is domestically supplied. No growth_yoy or cagr_forecast DataPoint exists for the overall India skincare market, so growth direction cannot be assessed from current data at the segment level. IMARC's own notes on the market-size figure reference a forward-looking trajectory to US$18.38bn by 2034 (~7.49% CAGR), but this is a forecast from a LOW-confidence source, not an observed trend. A single-company data point (Minimalist, NET_REALISATION, MEDIUM confidence, FY24) shows revenue up from Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr - one D2C brand's growth, not the market. Most India skincare figures here are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates (IMARC, Grand View Research, MarkNtel, IMA Pro) rather than primary-sourced, and none states organised-vs-unorganised coverage explicitly; several retail-price points are individual K-beauty SKUs [CORRIDOR], not market-wide figures.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (Korea vs India)
passages.text: A like-for-like size comparison is possible here because both sides carry a value_usd_bn figure on a RETAIL basis: Korea's domestic retail market converts to ~US$5.18bn (2025, HIGH confidence) versus India's ~US$9.06bn (2025, LOW confidence) - India reads larger on this comparison, though the confidence gap (HIGH vs LOW) means it should be treated as indicative, not precise. Korea's US$8.54bn EXPORT_FOB export figure sits on a different value_basis and cannot be netted against India's retail figure. The Korea-to-India corridor is real but small and inconsistent between reporting sides: Korea reports US$0.0656bn of HS 3304 (skincare plus makeup) exports to India in 2024 [CORRIDOR], while India reports US$0.140bn of HS 3304 imports from Korea in the same year [CORRIDOR] - a mismatch consistent with FOB-vs-CIF differences and mirror-trade-statistics discrepancies, and neither figure isolates skincare from makeup. A substantial set of individual K-beauty SKU retail prices captured from Nykaa and Blinkit (COSRX, Laneige, Innisfree, Anua, Beauty of Joseon, and others) document this corridor at the shelf level, but these are product-level price points, not a market-size figure for the corridor itself.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's sun-care segment now has a domestic anchor, but the cleanest figure is a production measure, not a retail one: MFDS sunscreen production value of KRW 0.47tn for CY2025 (MEDIUM confidence, PRODUCTION basis), which is factory-gate output and must not be read as domestic retail sell-through. Retail-basis market sizes are two conflicting LOW-confidence aggregator estimates — Grand View US$330mn (2024) versus MarkNtel US$747mn (2025), roughly a 2.3x spread. Reported SPF penetration is high but also conflicting (45% to 75%, both LOW). MFDS production grew +9.4% YoY in CY2025 (observed, MEDIUM, PRODUCTION basis). Forecast retail CAGRs sit between 3.59% (MarkNtel) and 8.3% (Grand View), both LOW. A separately reported +43% figure (Samsung Securities via Korea Herald) is a 2025 projection tied to overseas/e-commerce sales, not domestic retail growth. The strongest figure (MFDS) is on a PRODUCTION basis and is not comparable to retail sizes; the two retail estimates are LOW-confidence aggregator numbers about 2.3x apart, so absolute domestic scale remains uncertain.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (India)
passages.text: India sun care sizes at roughly US$0.58bn (IMARC, 2025) to US$0.89bn (TechSci, 2024) on a RETAIL basis, both LOW confidence — and these are effectively sunscreen-only sizings, which the segment-level figure already on file was built from. Sub-segment sun_protection now carries its own explicit sizings from the same houses, plus a MEDIUM-confidence K-beauty shelf-price point (Beauty of Joseon, Rs1570 MRP, [CORRIDOR]-tagged). Forecast CAGRs cluster 6.0-6.8% (IMARC, TechSci; LOW). The eye-catching +170% (2026) and +85% (2023) growth figures are quick-commerce channel and Nykaa-platform reads respectively (LOW/MEDIUM), not whole-segment growth — the category is surging on q-commerce off a small base, which is not the same as the segment growing that fast. Every size figure is a LOW aggregator estimate with a wide (~1.5x) spread and a sunscreen-only definition; the high growth numbers are channel-specific, not segment-wide, and must not be read as the market's overall rate.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional size comparison is possible: India's sunscreen market (~US$0.58-0.89bn) is broadly comparable to, and probably somewhat larger than, Korea's retail sunscreen (~US$0.33-0.75bn) — but every figure on both sides is LOW confidence with a ~2x internal spread, so this is directional only, not a firm ranking. Korea's most reliable datapoint is production (KRW 0.47tn, MEDIUM), a different basis that cannot be set against India's retail figures. On the corridor, sun care is baseline whitespace #2: Nykaa sunscreen grew +85% YoY and Korean-sunscreen searches +148%, evidencing real K-beauty sunscreen pull into India even though no corridor-specific market size exists yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's whole BPC market is anchored on a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor RETAIL figure of $13.0bn (2024), alongside a separately HIGH-confidence export figure of $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB (2025, MFDS/Korea Customs) - these sit on different value bases (domestic sell-through vs FOB shipments abroad) and are not additive. Per-capita spend of ~$250 (2024) is labelled an ESTIMATE derived in the baseline report, not a directly sourced figure. Two lower-confidence retail readings from Mordor Intelligence ($13.66bn, 2025) and Expert Market Research ($18.39bn, 2025) use a broader 'cosmetics' definition and are flagged value_basis_uncertain, so they sit alongside rather than override the Euromonitor anchor. Observed domestic retail growth was a modest 1.8% YoY in constant-value terms (2024, HIGH confidence, Euromonitor), while export growth ran far hotter at +12.3% YoY (2025) and +20.3% YoY (2024), both HIGH confidence. A LOW-confidence Mordor Intelligence figure forecasts 6.61% CAGR for 2025-2030 - a forecast, not an observed rate, and tied to a broader product basket than the headline retail size. The HIGH-confidence retail total and the HIGH-confidence export total both look solid individually but measure different things and must not be combined or netted; the only forward-looking growth figure (CAGR) carries LOW confidence and a wider product definition than the headline market size.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (India)
passages.text: India's whole BPC market is sized at $33.08bn (2025) on a MEDIUM-confidence Statista/China Briefing RETAIL basis that the underlying data itself flags as value_basis_uncertain; no export figure exists at the India headline level. Per-capita spend of $22.74 (2025, MEDIUM confidence) is roughly an order of magnitude below Korea's, consistent with a much larger population base spreading the same order-of-magnitude-larger market size. Observed growth is quoted at 10.0% YoY (2024) from a LOW-confidence baseline consensus that itself notes a spread across research houses (most cluster 10-11%, some conservative ones 5-6%). The cagr_forecast of 3.48% (2025-2030, MEDIUM confidence, Statista) is a forecast only, and is notably more conservative than both the observed 10% figure and the ~10% consensus the source itself references - implying an expected deceleration versus recent history. The headline market-size figure is MEDIUM confidence and explicitly flagged value-basis-uncertain (a Statista 'consumer market revenue' read, not a confirmed RETAIL sell-through number), and there is no export or independent per-capita cross-check at the headline level.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both headline market-size figures carry a value_usd_bn on a RETAIL basis, so a direct size comparison is possible: India's whole BPC market ($33.08bn, MEDIUM confidence, 2025) is roughly two and a half times the size of Korea's ($13.0bn, HIGH confidence, 2024), though the reference years differ by one and the confidence levels differ. Korea additionally carries a HIGH-confidence $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB total with no India counterpart in the headline data, so exports cannot enter this comparison. Both geographies show the same reconciliation tension: neither's top-down retail figure can be checked against its bottom-up sum, because the bottom-up bases differ in currency/unit and use NET_REALISATION rather than RETAIL, and in both cases that bottom-up sum is inflated by non-pure-play conglomerates reporting revenue well beyond BPC (LG H&H in Korea; Hindustan Unilever and Godrej Consumer Products in India) - both reconciliations are marked not publishable, with gap_pct left uncomputed rather than estimated. The Korea-India corridor does not appear in either headline block, but the raw data shows Korea's exports to India are a small, fast-growing slice (~$50m in H1 2025, +44.7% YoY) and several LOW/MEDIUM-confidence India-side estimates size the K-beauty-in-India [CORRIDOR] subset at roughly $0.3-0.4bn with high forecast CAGRs (19-26%, sources vary) - a fast-growing niche within, not representative of, either whole market.

passages.title: Corridor vector — read
passages.text: The Korea to India corridor is an import-and-curate entry route, not a build route: even AmorePacific is scaling India through platforms and imports with no India plant announced. The trade base is small but fast — baseline ~US$50m (H1 2025), +44.7% YoY — and HS 3304 imports from Korea were US$140m in 2024 (Comtrade, HIGH). Demand is proven at the platform layer (K-beauty GMV on Nykaa +60% YoY Jul-Sep 2025) and the K-beauty India market is put at ~INR 3,139cr (2025) with a ~26% CAGR to 2035 (single aggregator). A 2026 launch wave (Medicube, Illiyoon, TirTir, Hince, Dr. Melaxin) shows the corridor is actively widening. The entry decision therefore reduces to conduit choice plus clearing CDSCO — the numbers say demand and momentum are real, the friction is regulatory lead-time, and the whitespace is getting indie/derma K-beauty onto the Tier 2/3 rail rather than adding another conglomerate brand where the majors already sit.

passages.title: Corridor vector — whitespace_read
passages.text: The sharpest gap is mid-price derma K-beauty on the Tier 2/3 q-commerce rail (baseline whitespace #5, highest corridor conviction). The Blinkit snapshot makes it concrete: conglomerate-owned K-brands (AmorePacific, LG H&H) have mature India supply chains and are deeply stocked, while the indie/derma brands actually driving the K-beauty story (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, coming-soon or absent. The opportunity is not adding another conglomerate SKU where the majors already sit; it is getting masstige-price indie derma into dark-store distribution. Dedicated sunscreens (whitespace #2) and men's K-beauty (whitespace #4) are the adjacent gaps.

passages.title: Corridor vector — friction_read
passages.text: The binding friction is CDSCO import registration: a Form COS-1 application resolving to a COS-2 Registration Certificate via the SUGAM portal, required as pre-clearance before any consignment, plus manufacturing-site registration and BIS IS 4707 ingredient standards (Part 2 revised Aug 2025). Paper filings are no longer accepted as of 2026. This is a lead-time and working-capital cost rather than a hard barrier, but it must be cleared before the first shipment — cost and timeline are not yet quantified in the data and remain a research-needed item.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Nykaa
passages.text: Primary conduit and the deepest Korean assortment in India: a 10-year AmorePacific partnership (2016-2026) plus a widening exclusives book (Illiyoon, Aestura, RYO, Mise En Scene) and now non-AmorePacific indie brands (TirTir, Medicube). It is the only conduit with a published corridor demand signal — K-beauty GMV +60% YoY Jul-Sep 2025 — and is the exclusive launch pad for the K-derma wave. First choice for a premium/derma entrant.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Tira
passages.text: Reliance Retail's omnichannel platform running an aggressive 2026 K-beauty sprint built on exclusives (Hince Jan-2026, Dr. Melaxin exclusive Jul-2026, Medicube Feb-2026, Mixsoon since 2024). Its exclusive-launch model makes it the strongest alternative to Nykaa for a brand wanting a differentiated shelf and Reliance's store + online reach, though no corridor GMV figure is published for it.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — q-commerce
passages.text: Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart are the Tier 2/3 access rail and the corridor's clearest whitespace, but the assortment is uneven: a single Blinkit snapshot (2026-07-23, 63 K-brand SKUs) shows conglomerate brands stocked deep (The Face Shop 21 SKUs, Laneige 16) while the viral indie/derma brands driving the narrative (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, 'coming soon' or absent. High strategic value, thin current execution for indie derma.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Flipkart
passages.text: Launched an international K-beauty portfolio (2025) weighted to indie brands (Beauty of Joseon, rom&nd, TirTir, Thank You Farmer). Broad indie reach at mass scale, but the evidence is a launch note only — no assortment depth, exclusives or demand signal recorded.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Amazon
passages.text: Carries a spread of indie K-brands (Anua, Some By Mi, Isntree, Dr.Jart+, Etude, The Face Shop). Useful for reach and long-tail discovery, but only a brand list is recorded — no exclusives, assortment depth or corridor demand data to rank it higher.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — skinification
passages.text: The active-ingredient logic of skincare is migrating into hair care: demand is moving from mass shampoo toward serums and scalp tonics carrying named actives, and the finding explicitly flags specialist D2C outpacing legacy FMCG. It reframes hair care as a treatment category rather than a cleansing one, which favours ingredient-led entrants over shelf-space incumbents. Note the underlying India hair-care sizing is LOW-confidence and internally conflicting (Mordor 4.73% vs IMARC 10.58% CAGR), so the direction is well-evidenced but the magnitude is not.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — glass-skin/K-beauty pull
passages.text: K-drama/K-pop-led aspiration is converting into category-specific search and transaction demand, concentrated in derma-adjacent skincare and sunscreen where the 'glass skin' aesthetic is most legible. This is the corridor's demand engine: it is documented as a channel signal (Nykaa GMV, platform search spikes) rather than an independent market size, and the K-beauty India totals rest on a single aggregator, so treat it as a strong directional pull with soft absolute sizing.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — access-led q-commerce shift
passages.text: Quick commerce has become the default access rail into Tier 2/3, turning beauty from an aspiration-led into an availability-led purchase. BPC is growing far faster on q-commerce than overall, which reshapes route-to-market: dark-store availability, not brand awareness, is becoming the binding constraint on volume. The GMV split is single-sourced and the sunscreen surge is a LOW-confidence projection, but the structural shift is corroborated across multiple Redseer reads.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — premiumization
passages.text: Willingness to pay is rising within categories, not just across them: premium and masstige tiers are the fastest-growing slices even inside value-conscious channels like q-commerce, and imports cluster at the premium/K-beauty end. The masstige-derma tier is the clearest quantified expression of this. The signal is qualitative-plus-LOW-confidence sizing, so it supports a premium-tier entry thesis without a defensible premium market-size number.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — men's grooming rise
passages.text: Men's grooming is the segment with the firmest India demand base in the set — a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor size growing ~9% — with the skincare sub-slice growing faster still. It is simultaneously flagged as corridor whitespace because men's skincare is underserved relative to toiletries. The size and growth are well-evidenced; the sub-slice CAGR and the whitespace read are softer, so the opportunity framing is stronger than any precise men's-skincare number.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — premiumization
passages.text: Korea's mature domestic skincare market (~+1% YoY) is growing almost entirely through premium active-ingredient derma: dermocosmetics is up ~13% on next-generation actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides). Value growth is coming from ingredient escalation inside a flat volume base, which is what feeds the export and corridor story. This is the best-evidenced driver in the set (both points Euromonitor HIGH), but it describes the source market, not an India demand pull.

The corridor's headline entry case: highest corridor tailwind and most open competition; the drags are unresolved sizing (~7x spread) and the CDSCO import friction the whitespace must clear. market_size_evidence: 2/5 — Scale is genuinely unresolved: a narrow Rx-adjacent read of US$0.28bn (P&S 2024) sits ~7x below a broad read of US$1.85bn (MarkWide 2026), with a masstige-only cut at US$65.55mn. A real segment, but the sizing spread is too wide to bank on.; growth_evidence: 4/5 — Strong momentum from several angles: Nykaa K-beauty GMV +60% YoY (MEDIUM, [CORRIDOR]), forecast CAGRs 10.3-14.6% (LOW), and Minimalist revenue +89% FY24. Fast-growing across narrow and masstige cuts.; competitive_openness: 4/5 — The most open, most contested India segment on the evidence: a derma-D2C boom (Minimalist Rs347cr, HUL acquisition at Rs2,955cr / 8.5x — the benchmark exit), fast masstige growth (14.6% CAGR), and Korean derma brands entering. This is the corridor's highest-conviction whitespace.; channel_access: 4/5 — Nykaa is the exclusive-conduit spine for the K-derma wave (Medicube, Illiyoon, Aestura launching 2026) with strong access there — though the q-commerce derma rail is itself the whitespace (COSRX out-of-stock, Anua 'coming soon' on Blinkit), so access is strong on platforms but still thin on q-commerce.; regulatory_friction: 2/5 — Higher friction than other IN segments because the K-derma opportunity rides the import route, where CDSCO registration (COS-1->COS-2 via SUGAM, site registration, no paper filings) is the binding, evidenced barrier and lead-time cost.; corridor_tailwind: 5/5 — The strongest corridor tailwind in the taxonomy: baseline whitespace #1 (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3, highest corridor conviction), Nykaa K-beauty GMV +60% YoY, and a wave of 2026 K-derma launches (Medicube, Illiyoon, Aestura, Dr. Melaxin) across Nykaa and Tira.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Two listed conglomerates (AmorePacific, LG H&H) both carry colour cosmetics, and a deep ODM base (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) has enabled a long tail of indie brands (rom&nd, Etude, Hince) to proliferate and compete for the same shelf and export demand. Colour-cosmetics factory-gate output surged +51.4% YoY in 2024 (MFDS via Personal Care Insights, MEDIUM), a supply push that intensifies competition for placement. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. CJ Olive Young is the dominant health-and-beauty retail gatekeeper for Korean colour cosmetics (listed as the KR retailer conduit), giving concentrated channel leverage over brands, but no Korea-specific trade-margin or channel-share figure is in the repo to size that leverage precisely. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: No KR colour-cosmetics channel-concentration or trade-margin DataPoint exists; a retail-margin / Olive Young share figure would firm this rating.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea hosts three listed, competing ODM/OEM houses (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) plus a wider contract base, so brand owners can source formulation and fill from multiple suppliers on commodity terms. A fragmented, capable supplier tier keeps input-side bargaining power low for colour-cosmetics brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The same deep ODM base lets a new brand launch colour cosmetics without owning a factory, which is exactly how Korea's indie wave (rom&nd, Hince, Beauty of Joseon) reached market and then the corridor. MFDS registration exists but is not a scale barrier against the low formulation-and-fill cost of entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.text: No adjacent-segment substitution evidence for Korean colour cosmetics is present in the repo (e.g. no data on skincare-hybrids or tinted-care displacing makeup). passages.title: Porter overall — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea's colour cosmetics is a manufacturing-and-export hub with intense rivalry and easy entry (low supplier power, deep ODM base) but concentrated retail gatekeeping. Structurally crowded on the supply side; attractive as a sourcing/export origin rather than a low-competition domestic entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India colour cosmetics (US$3.46bn 2024, LOW) is mass-tier-dominated (79.55% mass share, Mordor 2025) and contested by MNC incumbents (HUL, L'Oreal India), platform-native D2C (SUGAR, Plum), and active strategic consolidation (HUL acquiring Minimalist and Plum). A crowded mass base plus M&A land-grab signals high competitive intensity. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Beauty platforms take the highest commission band of any category on colour cosmetics — Nykaa 24-28% — and concentrated q-commerce (Blinkit ~45-50%) is now a default access rail, so a small number of channel gatekeepers set the terms of shelf access and economics for entrants. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Indian brands overwhelmingly use third-party contract manufacturers / private-label houses (MOQs from ~500 units) rather than owning production, and specialty inputs come from established suppliers (Galaxy Surfactants, Fine Organics). A fragmented, agile CM base keeps supplier bargaining power low for colour brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Low production barriers (contract manufacturing) plus a strong D2C funding record (~US$757m into India beauty/wellness D2C over 18 months) make brand launch cheap and well-capitalised. CDSCO import registration (COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM) is a real barrier only for imported entrants, not domestic launches. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: No adjacent-segment substitution evidence for India colour cosmetics is present in the repo. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution read requires adjacent-segment evidence (e.g. tinted skincare / BB-CC displacement of colour makeup) not in current data.

passages.title: Porter overall — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India colour cosmetics is large and growing (forecast ~7-8% CAGR) with easy production-side entry, but rivalry is high, channel gatekeepers extract the category's top commission band, and incumbents are consolidating the best D2C assets. Attractive on size and growth, but not a low-competition or low-channel-cost entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. No derma-specific brand shares exist, but the visible competitive cluster is dense and the pull is strong: the segment grew +13% YoY (2024, Euromonitor, HIGH) on an actives race (PDRN, exosomes, peptides), and the named players span both majors and indies — AmorePacific runs Aestura and Illiyoon, LG H&H is present, and APR (Medicube) is a listed indie, alongside Dr.Jart+ and Dr. Melaxin. Double-digit growth attracting both conglomerate derma lines and funded indies into an actives arms race reads as HIGH rivalry, though the rating rests on player visibility rather than measured shares. Evidence strength: PARTIAL. Research needed: KR dermocosmetics brand-level shares (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter buyer power — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Derma reaches consumers through the same concentrated H&B retail (Olive Young) and online channels as skincare, plus pharmacy/clinic-adjacent routes, so channel power is present. No derma-specific channel-share or margin DataPoint exists, so the level is held at MEDIUM on structural inference. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR dermocosmetics channel mix and margins incl. pharmacy/clinic (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter supplier power — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's ODM base (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) extends into actives-heavy derma formulation, keeping the make outsourced and switchable and supplier leverage low overall. The one caveat: the frontier actives driving the segment (PDRN, exosomes, peptides) can concentrate around specialised ingredient/IP suppliers, which could raise supplier power at the premium edge — but the repo has no DataPoint isolating that, so the base reading stays LOW. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Whether frontier-actives (PDRN/exosome) supply is concentrated enough to lift supplier power (tavily, euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Cosmeceutical/derma positioning leans on efficacy claims that fall under MFDS functional-cosmetic approval — a higher regulatory bar than plain skincare — which restrains entry. Offsetting it, APR/Medicube shows a listed indie can scale a derma brand fast off the ODM base. The two forces net to MEDIUM. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: MFDS functional-cosmetic (derma-claim) approval cost/timeline (korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter substitutes — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: The natural adjacency is aesthetic-clinic procedures and injectables (the same PDRN/exosome science originates there), but the repo holds no DataPoint measuring substitution between dermocosmetics and procedures. Left unrated per the grounding rules. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution evidence between derma cosmetics and aesthetic/clinic procedures in KR (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: The fastest-growing KR segment on file (+13%, HIGH) with an active innovation frontier and low supplier power — genuinely dynamic — but sizing is definitionally unresolved (Korean sources ~4x apart) and the functional-cosmetic entry bar plus concentrated retail temper attractiveness. Strongest read is as a brand-incubation and corridor-export segment rather than a clean domestic-share play. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Derma/actives is India's hottest skincare fight. Domestic D2C is proven and consolidating — Minimalist reached Rs347cr revenue FY24 (+89% YoY) and was acquired by HUL at ~8.5x (~US$350mn), the benchmark derma-D2C exit — while the masstige-derma tier is the fastest-growing India cut on file (+14.6% CAGR). On top sit incumbents (Cetaphil, Skinshine) and an incoming K-derma import wave (Medicube, Aestura, Illiyoon on Nykaa/Tira). Multiple funded challengers, active M&A, and imports converging on one lane is HIGH rivalry. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Buyer power is elevated by conduit concentration specific to derma: Nykaa is effectively the exclusive gateway for the K-derma wave (Medicube omnichannel launch, Illiyoon exclusive, Aestura), and its K-beauty GMV grew +60% YoY (Q3 2025) — the platform sits astride the segment's fastest-growing supply. Add the concentrated q-commerce rail and standard commissions/MRP margins, and channel buyers hold strong leverage over derma brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Domestic derma D2C uses the same commoditised contract-manufacturing base as skincare (Gorgeous Cosmos / IndiaMART CMs; Galaxy Surfactants and Fine Organics for actives/surfactants), so suppliers hold little power over Indian brand owners. For imported K-derma the balance inverts — the brand depends on the Korean ODM/owner plus CDSCO clearance — so supplier power is MEDIUM specifically on the corridor-import lane. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Derma is the most-funded and most-imitated lane: the Minimalist exit set a benchmark that pulls capital in, masstige derma is growing +14.6%, and the house-of-brands model spins up derma sub-brands cheaply (Innovist's Chemist at Play) on commoditised CM. K-derma owners are also entering directly (APR launched Medicube; AmorePacific brought Illiyoon). The import lane carries CDSCO/BIS friction (MEDIUM there), but domestic and direct-K entry are both wide open. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: P&S scopes India dermacosmetics as Rx-adjacent (acne, psoriasis, scars), which points to dermatologist prescriptions and clinic treatment as the natural substitute — but no DataPoint measures that substitution flow, so the force is left unrated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution evidence: OTC dermocosmetics vs dermatologist Rx / clinic procedures in India (tavily, euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter overall — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: The corridor's highest-conviction whitespace — mid-price derma K-beauty into Tier 2/3 — and the most attractive of the three IN reads on demand: double-digit growth, a proven exit multiple, and confirmed corridor pull (Nykaa K-beauty GMV +60%, Medicube/Illiyoon/Aestura launching). Attractiveness is real but bounded by HIGH rivalry, HIGH buyer power (Nykaa's derma gatekeeping), and a genuinely unresolved ~7x sizing spread. Entry logic favours the corridor-import / partner-with-conduit route the whitespace itself describes. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India fragrances (~US$2.6bn perfume+deodorant, LOW) is led in mass by Vini Cosmetics/Fogg (FY25 revenue INR 1,200cr, KKR-controlled) with many domestic deo/perfume players, while a wave of D2C fragrance entrants is drawing investor money. A dominant mass player plus an active D2C challenger field indicates high intensity. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Premium/perfume distribution runs through beauty platforms taking Nykaa fragrance commission of 22-25%, while mass deodorant flows through fragmented GT/MT. Channel leverage is meaningful at the premium end but diluted across mass retail. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Premium fragrance is import-reliant — UAE is India's largest perfume-import source (HS 3303), then France/Germany for high-end oils — so premium entrants depend on overseas suppliers of oils and finished juice, raising input-side leverage. Mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled, so the higher supplier power is scoped to the premium tier. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled via contract manufacturing and D2C fragrance is actively funded, so domestic launch is cheap and well-capitalised. Premium entrants instead face import friction (CDSCO COS-1 to COS-2 plus overseas oil sourcing), so the threat is high for domestic-fill entrants and moderated for import-led premium. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The segment itself bundles fine perfume with deodorant/body-mist, and the dominant volume sits in cheaper deo/mist formats — evidencing substitution between premium perfume and mass deodorant within the same demand space. Substitution is directional given the combined-basket sizing. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter overall — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India fragrances is a growing, mass-led market with a dominant deo incumbent (Fogg) and easy domestic entry, but the premium tier an import-led K-beauty entrant would target is supplier-dependent (UAE/France) and channel-gated. Attractive on demand, but premium entry carries import and supplier friction; the KR-IN corridor flow itself is negligible. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea's US$1.8bn hair-care market (IMARC 2025, LOW) is anchored by AmorePacific (Mise En Scene, RYO) and LG H&H, with the ODM base enabling additional brands. Evidence is a single LOW size figure with no segment-specific shares, so intensity is inferred from the two-conglomerate structure rather than measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: No KR hair-care segment shares on file; brand-level share data would firm the rivalry read.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. CJ Olive Young and online are the concentrated KR retail channels, giving gatekeeper leverage, but no KR hair-care trade-margin or channel-share figure exists in the repo to size it. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR hair-care channel-concentration / retail-margin DataPoint absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's three listed ODM/OEM houses (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) and wider contract base supply hair-care formulation as readily as skincare, so brand owners face little input-side bargaining leverage. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The ODM base lets new hair-care brands launch asset-light, the same route by which AmorePacific's hair brands and indie labels reach shelf and the corridor. No scale barrier is evident for domestic entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — hair care (South Korea)

passages.title: Porter overall — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea hair care is a modest, two-conglomerate market with low supplier power and easy entry but thin repo evidence on shares and channel. Attractive as a source of formulation and corridor SKUs rather than a well-characterised domestic entry. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India hair care (~US$4.1bn 2026, LOW) is one of the largest BPC categories and is dominated by FMCG incumbents (HUL, Godrej) in shampoo/oils while actives-led D2C (Honasa, Innovist's Bare Anatomy) contest the premium 'skinification' edge, where specialist brands are cited as outperforming legacy FMCG. Broad incumbent scale plus D2C disruption yields high intensity. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Channel power is split: mass shampoo/oils flow through fragmented GT/MT where no single retailer dominates, while premium D2C hair care depends on beauty platforms taking Nykaa haircare commission of 20-24% and concentrated q-commerce. Gatekeeper leverage is real at the premium/D2C edge but diluted across mass distribution. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Contract manufacturing dominates D2C production, and the surfactant input critical to shampoos/cleansers comes from established domestic suppliers (Galaxy Surfactants named directly). A fragmented, capable supply base keeps input-side leverage low. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Skinification is opening an actives-led premium lane where D2C entrants outperform incumbents, contract manufacturing makes launch asset-light, and beauty D2C funding remains strong. Entry into the serum/scalp-care edge is cheap and well-capitalised. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Within the hair-growth/scalp space, ingestible supplements are documented as growing at more than twice the pace of topicals, evidencing active substitution away from traditional topical hair care toward adjacent formats. Substitution pressure is present but scoped to the hair-loss/scalp sub-space. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter overall — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India hair care is large and growing with easy production-side entry, but incumbents own the mass base, the growth edge (skinification/serums) is already crowded with well-funded D2C, and substitution toward supplements is emerging. Attractive on size; competitive on the premium lane that suits a K-beauty entrant. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The ODM base makes asset-light men's-grooming launches straightforward, and the market's high per-capita intensity attracts entrants. No scale barrier to domestic entry is evident. Evidence strength: THIN.

Attractive as a source of proven men's-skincare formulation for the corridor rather than a well-characterised domestic entry. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India men's grooming (INR 186.3bn / ~US$1.94bn 2025, Euromonitor HIGH, +9%) is contested by FMCG incumbents in the largest baskets (haircare, deodorants) plus razors, while men's skincare and beard care — the fastest-growing, corridor-whitespace slices — draw new D2C entrants. Established incumbency plus an emerging challenger front makes intensity high. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. E-commerce is 30-35% of urban men's-grooming sales (online ~27% share, fastest-growing), so beauty platforms and q-commerce are increasingly decisive gatekeepers, while the mass balance still moves through fragmented GT/MT. Channel leverage is rising but not yet dominant across the whole basket. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Men's-grooming D2C relies on the same fragmented third-party contract-manufacturing base (MOQs ~500 units) and domestic ingredient suppliers, so input-side bargaining power over brand owners is low. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Men's skincare is explicitly the corridor's whitespace #4 (underserved vs toiletries) and is the fastest-growing slice, so an underserved, growing lane sits open to asset-light contract-manufactured D2C and to K-beauty import entrants — with CDSCO registration the main friction for the imported route. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Men's-dedicated products compete with unisex/family grooming and the basket is shifting from toiletries toward skincare — men trading traditional shave/toiletry spend into dedicated skincare and beard care evidences substitution within the segment. Directional, given basket-definition variance. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter overall — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India men's grooming is well-evidenced, growing +9%, with low supplier power and an explicit, underserved men's-skincare whitespace (corridor #4) that suits a K-beauty entrant. But incumbents own the large toiletries/deo/hair baskets, rivalry is high, and rising channel concentration adds gatekeeper cost. Attractive on the skincare whitespace specifically rather than the broad basket. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Two listed conglomerates split the organised top (LG H&H 59.9%, AmorePacific 40.1% of the summed listed-brand-owner base, 2025), but that share cut deliberately excludes an unusually deep indie long tail — COSRX, Anua (The Founders), Beauty of Joseon (Gudai Global), TirTir and APR/Medicube all compete visibly and several are recent entrants. A domestic retail market growing only +1% YoY (HIGH) against skincare-led exports up +11.6% YoY (HIGH, world #2 cosmetics exporter) means players fight over a near-flat home market while racing overseas. That combination — concentrated majors plus a crowded, fast-refreshing indie field in a stagnant domestic pool — is high rivalry. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. CJ Olive Young is the dominant health-and-beauty retail gatekeeper for domestic sell-through, and duty-free is a distinct, powerful channel (now contracting on the Chinese daigou decline) — both concentrate distribution in few hands, which raises buyer/channel power over brands. But the repo carries no numeric KR channel-share or retail-margin DataPoint, so the level is inferred from channel structure rather than measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Olive Young / online / duty-free channel shares and retail trade margins for KR skincare (euromonitor_passport, korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter supplier power — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's brand-formulation supply is a deep, competitive ODM/OEM ecosystem — Cosmax, Kolmar Korea and Cosmecca Korea are all listed, scaled contract manufacturers. That commoditises production, lets a brand owner outsource the whole make with low switching cost, and is precisely what enables the indie proliferation seen in rivalry. Suppliers therefore hold little pricing leverage over brands. Rated on structural presence of the ODM base rather than on any margin/cost DataPoint. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The same ODM depth that suppresses supplier power collapses the capital barrier to launching a skincare brand, and the recent arrival of indie names now carried across India's conduits (Anua, Beauty of Joseon, TirTir) evidences a live, low-friction entry pipeline. General (non-functional) skincare carries only light MFDS notification, not efficacy approval, so the regulatory gate is modest for basic-skincare entrants. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: No DataPoint in the repo measures cross-category substitution away from KR skincare (e.g. toward aesthetic procedures or colour cosmetics). Per the grounding rules this force is left unrated rather than guessed. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Evidence on substitution between skincare routines and aesthetic/derma procedures in KR (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Structurally unattractive for a share-seeking entrant: a near-flat domestic market (+1%) with concentrated majors, a churning indie field, and near-zero barriers to entry compresses domestic economics. The real value of the KR skincare complex is as a brand-incubation and export engine (+11.6% exports, world #2), not as a domestic-share prize. Rivalry HIGH and new-entrant threat HIGH are the binding forces; low supplier power is the enabling condition, not an advantage a newcomer can capture. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Organised skincare is dominated at the top by non-pure-play FMCG (HUL 78.6%, Godrej 18.5%, Honasa 2.9% of the listed-brand-owner base) but is being contested underneath by a large D2C insurgency and heavy consolidation — HUL acquired Minimalist (~Rs3,000cr, 8.5x revenue) and Plum, Estee took Forest Essentials, Puig took Kama Ayurveda, KKR took Vini. A 40% mass-tier share (<Rs200: Pond's, Nivea, Himalaya, Lakme, Garnier) sits alongside a premiumising K-beauty import layer. Concentrated incumbents plus a well-funded, consolidating challenger field is high rivalry. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Distribution power sits with a concentrated set of platforms and gatekeepers. Nykaa charges 22-26% commission on skincare brands (plus 18% GST on top); the q-commerce access rail is concentrated in three players (Blinkit ~45-50%, Zepto ~20-25%, Instamart ~20-25%); and India MRP embeds a 25-45% trade margin per the repo's normalisation rule. Brands face powerful, few buyers between them and the shelf. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. India D2C skincare rarely owns factories — brands use third-party contract manufacturers / private-label houses (Gorgeous Cosmos and hundreds on IndiaMART, MOQs from ~500 units), with specialty inputs from domestic suppliers (Galaxy Surfactants, Fine Organics). Manufacturing is commoditised and switchable, and the market is ~91% domestically supplied by value, so suppliers hold little leverage over brand owners. (Imported K-beauty inverts this — see the corridor note in new-entrant threat.) Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Domestic entry is cheap and live: commoditised contract manufacturing plus continuing funding (~US$757m into India D2C beauty/wellness over 18 months; KOSE into Foxtale, Moxie, Antinorm) and a house-of-brands model (Innovist's Chemist at Play) keep new brands arriving despite the D2C slowdown. The offsetting friction applies only to imports — any imported cosmetic needs CDSCO registration (Form COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM) plus site registration and BIS IS 4707 compliance — so the import lane is MEDIUM while the domestic lane is HIGH. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — skincare (India)
passages.text: No DataPoint measures substitution pressure on India skincare specifically. Skinification of hair care (actives migrating into serums/tonics) is documented as category-blurring but is adjacency, not evidence that another category displaces facial skincare. Left unrated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution evidence for India skincare vs adjacent actives categories (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — skincare (India)
passages.text: Attractive on size and growth (US$9.06bn, 2025; consolidation confirming value) but hard to enter unaided: rivalry is HIGH across both incumbents and D2C, and buyer power is HIGH because platform gatekeepers (Nykaa, q-commerce trio) and MRP trade margins tax every brand. Low supplier power favours an asset-light build, but the import lane's CDSCO friction and the platforms' leverage argue for a partner-with-conduit / corridor-import route over a cold domestic launch. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. No sun-care-specific brand shares exist in the repo, so rivalry is inferred from segment structure. Korea is a global sunscreen production and export force — MFDS sunscreen production value KRW 470.3bn (CY2025, +9.4%), Kolmar Korea's US-bound OTC sunscreen +88% (2024), Korean sun-care US e-commerce projected +43% (2025) — which signals many capable, competing manufacturers/brands rather than a settled domestic oligopoly. Absent domestic share counts, the level is held at MEDIUM: clearly contested and innovation-driven, but the underlying rivalry intensity for domestic sell-through is not measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR sun-care domestic brand shares / player count (euromonitor_passport, korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter buyer power — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The channel structure mirrors KR skincare — Olive Young as dominant H&B gatekeeper, online, and duty-free — so channel/buyer concentration is present, but there is no sun-care-specific channel-share or margin DataPoint. Held at MEDIUM on structural inference only. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR sun-care channel shares and retail margins (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter supplier power — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Sunscreen is manufacturing- and formulation-intensive, yet Korea's ODM base specialises in exactly this — Kolmar Korea is named directly as the OTC-sunscreen contract manufacturer behind the US export surge, alongside Cosmax and Cosmecca. A deep, competitive sunscreen-capable ODM ecosystem keeps supplier leverage over brands low and switching feasible. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Sunscreen is a 'functional cosmetic' under MFDS — it sits inside the functional-cosmetics production category (KRW 7.18tn, 40% of total) that requires efficacy/SPF approval, a real gate above plain-skincare notification. That approval bar tempers the otherwise-HIGH entry threat that Korea's ODM depth would create, netting to MEDIUM. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: MFDS functional-cosmetic sunscreen approval cost/timeline (korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter substitutes — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: No DataPoint measures substitution of dedicated KR sunscreen by SPF-moisturisers, cushions or make-up-with-SPF. Left unrated rather than guessed. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Evidence on SPF-moisturiser / SPF-make-up substitution for dedicated sunscreen in KR (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter overall — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: KR sun care reads as a production/export strength rather than a domestic-share opportunity: an efficacy-regulated 'functional cosmetic' with a deep sunscreen-capable ODM base (low supplier power) that is dynamic on exports (+9.4% production, +88% Kolmar US OTC, +43% US e-commerce). Its attractiveness to an entrant is as a sourcing and corridor-export base; the domestic scale itself is uncertain (retail estimates span 2.3x, all LOW). Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The market is small and underpenetrated (US$0.58-0.89bn, 2024-25; only ~32.77% of surveyed Indians used sun care daily, 2019) but actively contested — legacy players compete with a wave of D2C sun-specialists (e.g. Innovist's Sunscoop) and a growing K-beauty import layer where Beauty of Joseon's SPF50+ is a category bestseller. Fragmentation over a still-small base reads as MEDIUM rivalry, not the HIGH seen in mainstream skincare. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Sunscreen is a q-commerce hero category, which puts unusual leverage in the platforms' hands: q-commerce sunscreen is projected ~+170% in 2026 and Nykaa's platform sunscreen sales grew +85% YoY (2023). With the access rail concentrated in Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart and Nykaa, plus standard commissions and MRP trade margins, channel buyers hold strong power over sun-care brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Sunscreen brands draw on the same commoditised Indian contract-manufacturing and specialty-ingredient base as skincare (Gorgeous Cosmos / IndiaMART CMs, Galaxy Surfactants, Fine Organics). SPF formulation and BIS IS 4707 testing add some technical demand on the supplier, but do not concentrate supply enough to give manufacturers pricing power over brands. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Dedicated sunscreens are baseline whitespace #2 (India sun care underpenetrated), the q-commerce surge lowers the access barrier for new brands into Tier 2/3, and cheap contract manufacturing plus live D2C funding keep domestic launches easy (Innovist's Sunscoop is a documented sun-specialist entrant). Imports face the CDSCO + BIS SPF gate (MEDIUM for that lane), but the domestic and corridor entry vectors are wide open. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The dominant alternative to dedicated sunscreen in India is non-consumption and casual substitution: a 2019 survey found 25.62% never use sun care and only ~32.77% use it daily, so SPF-moisturisers, BB creams and simply going without still absorb much of the occasion. That non-consumption pool is the real competitor for a dedicated-sunscreen entrant, though the supporting datapoint is a single dated survey. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Current substitution split: dedicated sunscreen vs SPF-moisturiser/BB vs non-use in India (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — sun care (India)
passages.text: The most corridor-favourable of the three segments on the demand side: underpenetrated, high-growth, and pulled by evidenced K-beauty sunscreen demand (Korean-sunscreen searches +148%, glass-skin +61%). Attractive for entry on growth + corridor tailwind, but tempered by a small base, HIGH buyer power (q-commerce/Nykaa gatekeeping of the hero category), and non-consumption as the standing alternative. Best pursued via the corridor-import / partner-with-conduit route that the whitespace itself implies. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.
