passages.title: Price ladder — masstige gap
passages.text: The observed India ladder is barbelled. Mass sits at Rs500-700 (India D2C serum), and imported K-beauty premium sits at Rs2000-2999 (Anua toner, large-format Innisfree). Between them, the Rs700-1600 masstige band is populated almost entirely by K-beauty SKUs that reach it only through heavy promotion — COSRX essence lists at Rs1490 MRP but sells at Rs969; Innisfree's small serum lands at Rs680 on Blinkit; The Face Show/Laneige/Etude q-commerce SKUs sit Rs600-1600. This is precisely the corridor's opening: mid-price derma K-beauty at a genuine (not promo-dependent) Rs700-1500 shelf price on the q-commerce rail into Tier 2/3 (baseline whitespace #5). The MRP-vs-promoted spread is the tell — brands are papering the masstige gap with discounts on premium-listed SKUs rather than pricing a true masstige tier, which an entrant with lower landed cost (e.g. India-manufactured Korean-ingredient line) could occupy directly.

passages.title: Risk — data-confidence (BOTH)
passages.text: Severity HIGH. Most India segment sizes and growth rates rest on LOW-confidence aggregators (IMARC, TechSci, Mordor, P&S, MarkWide, EMR) and carry unresolved definitional gaps: India dermocosmetics spans a ~7x range (P&S US$256m 2023 vs MarkWide US$1.85bn 2026), sun care shows a ~2.3x base gap, and hair-care CAGR reads split 4.73% vs 10.58%. Korea's core skincare/derma/men's figures are Euromonitor HIGH, but several KR segments are export-value-only. Building an entry case on these numbers risks anchoring to a figure that is definitional noise, not signal. Mitigation: Lean on the HIGH-confidence anchors (Euromonitor KR retail, UN Comtrade trade flows, Euromonitor IN men's grooming) and treat aggregator CAGRs as scenario ranges, not point estimates. Apply the repo's >20% reconciliation gap rule: where top-down and bottom-up diverge, find the definitional mismatch before publishing a number. Flag every value_basis_uncertain item in the entry case.

passages.title: Risk — concentration (BOTH)
passages.text: Severity MEDIUM. The market-share reads are shares of only 2-3 listed brand owners each (KR: LG H&H, AmorePacific; IN: HUL, Godrej, Honasa), computed on NET_REALISATION revenue, excluding all unorganised/unlisted players, and inflated by non-pure-play conglomerates carrying non-BPC revenue. They are coverage indicators, not true category shares. Reading 'competitive openness' or rivalry directly off them would overstate incumbent dominance and misjudge how contestable a segment actually is. Mitigation: Read shares as coverage indicators, never as market shares; do not net conglomerate revenue against BPC-only sizes. Where a competitive-openness judgment is needed, ground it in channel and assortment evidence (conduit portfolios, q-commerce depth) rather than these share tables.

passages.title: Risk — regulatory (IN)
passages.text: Severity HIGH. Any imported cosmetic requires CDSCO import registration (Form COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM) as pre-clearance before any consignment, plus manufacturing-site registration and BIS IS 4707 compliance (Part 2 revised Aug 2025); paper filings are no longer accepted as of 2026. This gates the entire import_corridor thesis: no registration, no shipment. The severity is compounded because cost and timeline are not quantified anywhere in the current data. Mitigation: Budget CDSCO lead-time and working capital into any import_corridor plan and file registration well ahead of first shipment. Commission a regulatory pass (per the /regulatory backlog) to quantify COS-2 cost and timeline before committing volume. Where registration is a blocker, partner with a conduit that already holds registrations for the brand.

passages.title: Risk — FX pinning (BOTH)
passages.text: Severity MEDIUM. All USD normalisation is pinned to a single FX date (USD/KRW 1478.40, USD/INR 96.23, both 2026-07-21), and KR retail figures are converted via the inverse of that rate. Cross-geography comparisons and any KRW-cost / INR-revenue corridor margin are sensitive to rate drift away from that pin, so a comparison that looks clean today can move purely on FX. Mitigation: Re-pin FX each research pass and record the rate + date with every conversion; always show original currency alongside the USD equivalent; never net figures across value_basis, and flag corridor margin reads as FX-sensitive.

passages.title: Risk — single-source (BOTH)
passages.text: Severity MEDIUM. Several load-bearing figures rest on a single source with no triangulation: the corridor trade base (baseline report only), the q-commerce assortment picture (one Blinkit snapshot, 2026-07-23), the Nykaa K-beauty GMV growth (one earnings citation), the KR total market size (Euromonitor only) and the IN headline market size (Statista via China Briefing, value_basis uncertain). Any of these moving would shift the entry case, and none is currently corroborated. Mitigation: Triangulate each single-source figure with a second independent source before using it as load-bearing; re-run the q-commerce tracker on a schedule so the assortment read is a trend, not a one-off; keep value_basis_uncertain items explicitly labelled in the entry case.

passages.title: Route to market — e-commerce (India)
passages.text: India online BPC reached ~INR 56,000cr in FY26, growing ~35% YoY (Redseer, Habit or Desire); digital channels were ~9.4% of BPC revenue in 2025 (baseline, LOW); e-commerce is projected to reach 34-38% of ALL India BPC spend by 2030 (Redseer, Beauty Blitz 2030 — implying offline still holds ~62-66%). Beauty platforms Nykaa/Tira/Flipkart/Amazon are the K-beauty conduits: Nykaa runs the 10-year AmorePacific portfolio (Innisfree, Laneige, Sulwhasoo, COSRX, Aestura, Illiyoon) and now also carries independent K-brands (TirTir Jun-2026, Medicube); Reliance's Tira is on a 2026 exclusive-launch sprint (Hince Jan, Medicube Feb, Dr. Melaxin Jul). Platform commissions are steep — Nykaa 22-28% by category (skincare ~24%, colour ~26%; Sylvr); Amazon.in referral 7-10% above INR1,000 but 0% below INR1,000 effective Mar-2026 (KwickMetrics). Entry implication: The online rail is where a K-beauty entrant lands first: it is the fastest-growing channel and the established conduit for imported Korean SKUs, requiring no GT/MT distribution build. But platform economics are demanding — budget ~22-28% of sell-through to Nykaa, while Amazon's zero referral below INR1,000 tilts the maths toward entry-price hero SKUs. Conduit choice is a strategic fork: Nykaa's incumbent AmorePacific tie-up versus Tira's exclusive-launch land grab.

passages.title: Route to market — quick-commerce (India)
passages.text: Q-commerce is ~INR 40,000cr (~US$5bn) GMV in 2026, split roughly Blinkit 45-50% / Zepto 20-25% / Instamart 20-25% (Digital in Asia). BPC is the second-largest q-commerce category — ~8.5% of total q-commerce GMV in CY25, up from ~2.8% CY22; within online BPC, q-commerce rose to ~16% CY25 (from ~2% CY22) and ~18% FY26 (from 9% FY25) per Redseer. BPC GMV on q-commerce grew 120%+ YoY FY26 / ~140% CY25, and beauty on q-commerce +160% YoY (RedSeer via Unicommerce); BPC is ~13.4% of Blinkit's daily sales (Unicommerce). A live Blinkit capture (2026-07-23) shows the rail splits by ownership: conglomerate K-brands are deeply stocked (LG H&H's The Face Shop 21 SKUs, AmorePacific's Laneige 16 / Etude 10 / Innisfree 9), but the viral indie/derma brands driving the narrative are thin or absent (COSRX out-of-stock, Anua 'coming soon', Some By Mi / Isntree / Mixsoon absent). Take rates: Blinkit 18-22% base commission on MRP (~38% all-in incl. fulfilment/ads); Zepto ~22-23% (NewsBytes). Entry implication: Q-commerce is the access rail into Tier 2/3 and the corridor's clearest whitespace (baseline #5, mid-price derma K-beauty). The gap is not the conglomerate brands already on the shelf — it is getting indie/derma K-beauty onto dark-store slots. All-in economics (~38% on Blinkit) plus commission charged on MRP (not discounted price) mean an entrant must price for a high channel take. Dark-store SKU counts are small, so the play is a tight hero-SKU assortment, not a full range.

passages.title: Route to market — D2C (India)
passages.text: India's D2C beauty engine runs on third-party contract manufacturers (MOQs from ~500 units); the brand owns formula and brand, the CM owns production (Gorgeous Cosmos; hundreds on IndiaMART). Funding continues despite the broader D2C slowdown — ~US$757m into India D2C over 18 months (wellness+beauty led), with KOSE putting US$30m into Foxtale, Moxie raising US$15m and Antinorm an INR28cr seed (The D2C Pulse). D2C is projected to hold ~10% of online BPC by 2030 (Redseer). Indian D2C brands are already going Korean at local price points — Pilgrim's Korean Rice Water range, Limese (formulated in Korea for Indian skin), and Foxtale's Hula Hoop house-of-brands play (corridor.yaml india_side_players). Entry implication: A K-beauty entrant can side-step import registration entirely by building an India D2C line (own brand via contract manufacturer) — the Limese/Pilgrim template — trading corridor authenticity for speed, lower landed cost and no CDSCO COS-2 wait. Own-site D2C also escapes the 22-38% platform/q-commerce take, but must self-fund traffic. Deep contract-manufacturing capacity makes a made-in-India Korean-ingredient line feasible at mass Rs500-700 price points.

passages.title: Route to market — general trade (India)
passages.text: GT (kirana) still dominates Indian retail — offline is projected to retain ~62-66% of BPC even in 2030 (Redseer, Beauty Blitz 2030). Kirana margins run 5-10% on national brands with strong consumer pull but 18-25%+ demanded from NEW/unfamiliar brands; distributor all-in cost for smaller brands is 20-30% of sale price (Kirana Club). A Storewise worked example shows the structure — distributor/substockist ~12%, retailer ~20% on a mid-FMCG SKU. These are FMCG-wide benchmarks, not BPC-specific. Entry implication: GT is a heavy lift for an import-led K-beauty entrant: a new/unknown brand pays the top of the margin band (18-25%+ retailer, 20-30% distributor all-in) and needs a physical distributor network to reach kirana. It is not an entry channel — it is a scale channel to attempt only after online/q-commerce prove demand. Imported unit economics rarely survive GT margins stacked on top of CDSCO-landed cost.

passages.title: Route to market — modern trade (India)
passages.text: Modern-trade (organised chains, beauty specialty stores) evidence is thin — no modern-trade-specific BPC margin surfaced on any fetched page (explicitly noted in the trade-margin research). The nearest specialty-retail proxy is beauty platforms' own physical formats — Tira's select stores, used alongside online for K-beauty exclusive launches (corridor.yaml). Entry implication: research needed — insufficient standalone MT data to size the channel or its economics. For a K-beauty entrant, MT currently surfaces mainly as the physical arm of omnichannel platforms (Tira stores) rather than an independent route; treat it as an extension of the platform relationship until MT-specific data lands.

passages.title: Route to market summary (India)
passages.text: For a K-beauty entrant, India's route to market is online-first: e-commerce platforms (Nykaa/Tira/Flipkart/Amazon) are the proven conduit for imported Korean SKUs and the fastest-growing channel (~35% YoY), while quick-commerce (~US$5bn GMV, BPC growing 120-140% YoY) is the Tier 2/3 access rail and the corridor's clearest whitespace — specifically getting indie/derma K-beauty onto dark stores the conglomerate brands already occupy. Both online routes carry heavy take rates (Nykaa 22-28%, Blinkit ~38% all-in on MRP), so pricing must absorb the channel. D2C via contract manufacturing offers a CDSCO-free, lower-cost alternative at mass price points (the Limese/Pilgrim Korean-ingredient template). General trade is a post-proof scale channel where new brands pay punishing margins (18-30%), and modern trade lacks standalone data — research needed.

passages.title: Route to market — H&B stores (Olive Young) (South Korea)
passages.text: Health & beauty specialty stores are Korea's anchor beauty channel — Mordor puts them at ~54.1% of 2025 cosmetics distribution, led by CJ Olive Young, which holds MORE THAN 85% of the Korean H&B STORE market with 1,380+ stores (Seoulz). Olive Young standalone revenue was KRW 5.83tn (~US$4.2bn) in CY2025, +21.8% YoY (Seoulz); Daxue reports KRW 4.8tn consolidated 2024, +23.9% YoY. Notably, 26.4% of Olive Young's H1 2025 customers were foreign — tourist beauty spend is shifting out of duty-free and into H&B stores (Korea Times). Entry implication: Olive Young is the single most important shelf in Korea and a near-gatekeeper for domestic H&B distribution — winning it is close to winning the channel, but that dominance hands it strong buyer power over an entrant's terms and margins. Its rising foreign-customer share also makes it a discovery surface: a brand that proves out on Olive Young builds the reference to later travel the corridor to India.

passages.title: Route to market — online (e-commerce) (South Korea)
passages.text: Online is the largest channel by the Korea Ratings measure — 60.8% of the Korea cosmetics market in CY2024, up from 39.1% in 2019; Korea's online cosmetics transaction value was KRW 13.8tn (~US$9.25bn) in 2024, +7.7% YoY (Statistics Korea via press). This 60.8% online figure CONFLICTS with Mordor's 54.1% H&B-store share for 2025 — different channel definitions and coverage, so the two must not be added. Entry implication: E-commerce is either the largest or second-largest Korean channel depending on definition, and it grows steadily (~8% on online transaction value). For an entrant it is the lowest-barrier domestic route, but the definitional overlap with H&B means online and Olive Young should be treated as overlapping — not additive — when sizing reachable demand.

passages.title: Route to market — department store (South Korea)
passages.text: Department stores are the prestige tier of Korean beauty retail, but the available split combines them with drugstores: offline (department stores + drugstores) was 39.2% of the Korea cosmetics market in CY2024, down from 60.9% in 2019 (Korea Ratings) — a structural decline as online and H&B took share. The source does not break out a department-store-only figure. Entry implication: The prestige department-store channel is shrinking and is not separated out in the data, so it is a weak standalone entry route. It matters only for a premium-positioned brand; a masstige/derma K-beauty entrant should skip it in favour of H&B and online.

passages.title: Route to market — duty-free (distinct channel) (South Korea)
passages.text: Duty-free is a DISTINCT channel (repo rule 12 — never folded into domestic retail) and it is in structural decline: Korea duty-free sales were US$7.3bn Jan-Oct 2025, -16.6% YoY, headed for the lowest full year since 2015 (pre-pandemic >US$20bn/yr; AJU Press); KRW 6.36tn in H1 2025 (Korea Times). Figures cover all duty-free categories, not beauty only (cosmetics was historically the largest). The driver is the collapse of Chinese daigou/tourist buying, with the displaced tourist beauty spend migrating into Olive Young H&B stores. Entry implication: Duty-free is a declining, tourist-dependent channel an entrant should not build a Korea strategy around; its historic role as the daigou export back-door has broken down. Its decline is itself a signal — prioritise domestic H&B and online, where the displaced tourist demand is landing.

passages.title: Route to market summary (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's beauty distribution splits between two dominant domestic channels whose measured shares conflict by definition: H&B specialty stores (~54% per Mordor, anchored by Olive Young at >85% of the H&B store market and KRW 5.83tn revenue) and online (~61% per Korea Ratings, KRW 13.8tn transaction value) — the two overlap and must not be summed. For an entrant, Olive Young is the near-gatekeeper shelf and online the lowest-barrier route; both are also where displaced tourist demand is concentrating. Department stores are a shrinking prestige tier (only available combined with drugstores, ~39% offline) relevant to premium brands only. Duty-free is a distinct, structurally declining channel (US$7.3bn Jan-Oct 2025, -16.6% YoY) hollowed out by the daigou collapse — flagged separately and not to be built around.

passages.title: Value Chain — operating margins
passages.text: India brand-owner operating margins fan out sharply by model: legacy FMCG runs highest (Hindustan Unilever ~23%, Godrej Consumer ~21% FY26), the D2C challenger sits far lower (Honasa ~10%), and the pure retailer thinnest of all (Nykaa/FSN ~8%). The spread says the profit pool concentrates at scale-manufacturing incumbents; a new brand entering as a D2C or riding a retail platform should underwrite low-double-digit or single-digit operating margins, not FMCG-grade economics, at least until it earns scale.

passages.title: Value Chain — gross/trade margins
passages.text: Category gross margins are wide but heavily eroded downstream. A 30ml serum shows a 75-85% gross markup (COGS Rs80-120 vs MRP Rs500-700), yet the D2C Pulse itself flags that true margin falls sharply after packaging, shipping and returns. On the platform side, Nykaa takes roughly a 22-26% commission on skincare brands (~24% midpoint), higher for new brands. The headline gross margin is real but is not the margin an entrant keeps: platform commission plus fulfilment is the binding economic reality.

passages.title: Value Chain — import dependence
passages.text: India skincare is ~91% domestically supplied by value (imports ~US$844m against a ~US$9bn market), with imports concentrated in the premium and K-beauty tiers — Korea ~17% and China ~22% of skincare imports. HS 3304 imports from Korea were US$140m in 2024 (Comtrade, HIGH). Premium fragrance is the exception (import-reliant, UAE/France-led; ~12.8% dependence), while mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled. The read for a Korean entrant: you are competing in the ~9% import slice, not the whole market, and that slice is exactly where the corridor pull sits.

passages.title: Value Chain — contract manufacturing
passages.text: Most Indian D2C beauty brands own formula and brand but not factories — they run on third-party contract manufacturers / private-label houses (Gorgeous Cosmos and hundreds on IndiaMART) with MOQs from ~500 units. Two service models coexist: FMCG buyers demand audit-readiness and scale, D2C buyers demand agility, small batches and RM transparency. Upstream, Galaxy Surfactants (mild surfactants) and Fine Organics (specialty additives) anchor domestic actives supply. The implication is a genuinely low build barrier — an entrant can launch a domestic-made brand without capex — but differentiation then rests on formula and brand, not manufacturing.

passages.title: Value Chain — FX exposure
passages.text: Every cross-geography number in this system is pinned to a single FX date (USD/KRW 1478.40, USD/INR 96.23, both 2026-07-21), and Korean retail figures are converted via the inverse of that rate. For an importer running the corridor, this is a real operating exposure, not just a modelling artefact: COGS accrue in KRW while MRP is set in INR, so KRW appreciation compresses the landed margin between purchase and sale. Any USD-normalised comparison across the two markets inherits the same single-date sensitivity. This is an inference from the pinned-rate structure, not an observed FX-loss datapoint.

passages.title: India finding — supply chain
passages.text: Most Indian D2C beauty brands do NOT own factories — they use third-party contract manufacturers / private-label houses (e.g. Gorgeous Cosmos, and hundreds listed on IndiaMART), with MOQs from ~500 units. The brand owns formula/brand; the CM owns production. (Source: Gorgeous Cosmos; IndiaMART)

passages.title: India finding — supply chain
passages.text: FMCG brands demand audit-readiness/scale from CMs; D2C brands demand agility, small batches, and RM-sourcing transparency — two different contract-manufacturing service models. (Source: IMARC Engineering)

passages.title: India finding — supply chain
passages.text: Upstream, specialty-ingredient suppliers underpin the chain: Galaxy Surfactants (mild surfactants for cleansers) and Fine Organics (oleochemical specialty additives) are key Indian actives/ingredient makers. (Source: Marcellus; GlobalData)

passages.title: India finding — import make
passages.text: India skincare is ~91% domestically supplied by value (imports ~US$844m vs ~US$9bn market); imports concentrate in premium and K-beauty tiers. Korea 17% and China 22% of skincare imports. (Source: UN Comtrade; IMARC (derived))

passages.title: India finding — import make
passages.text: Premium fragrance is import-reliant: UAE is India's largest perfume-import source (HS 3303), then France/Germany for high-end oils; mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled. (Source: Seair Exim)

passages.title: India finding — import make
passages.text: Any imported cosmetic needs a CDSCO Import Registration (Form COS-1 -> COS-2 via SUGAM), plus manufacturing-site registration — the key lead-time/friction cost for K-beauty entrants. (Source: PSR Compliance / CDSCO)

passages.title: India finding — new players
passages.text: Consolidation by strategics: HUL acquired Minimalist (~Rs3,000cr) and Plum; Estee Lauder took Forest Essentials; Puig bought 85% of Kama Ayurveda; KKR owns 54% of Vini Cosmetics/Fogg (US$625m, US$1.2bn valuation). (Source: IMA Pro; Economic Times)

passages.title: India finding — new players
passages.text: Funding continues into 2026 despite the broader D2C slowdown: KOSE invested US$30m in Foxtale, Moxie raised US$15m, Antinorm Rs28cr seed; India D2C attracted ~US$757m over 18 months (wellness+beauty led). (Source: The D2C Pulse; The Hindu BusinessLine)

passages.title: India finding — new players
passages.text: House-of-brands model emerging among small players: Innovist runs Bare Anatomy (hair), Chemist at Play (skin), Sunscoop (sun) as science-backed sub-brands. (Source: Indian Startup Times)

passages.title: India finding — new players
passages.text: K-beauty brand owners are entering directly: APR launched Medicube on Nykaa; AmorePacific introduced dermocosmetic brand Illiyoon — accelerating India entry to offset SWANA-region volatility. (Source: Personal Care Insights)

passages.title: India finding — demand
passages.text: Beauty is one of the fastest-rising quick-commerce categories: ~160% YoY growth (RedSeer); premium/high-end beauty is gaining on q-commerce, not just mass. (Source: RedSeer (via Unicommerce))

passages.title: India finding — demand
passages.text: Q-commerce is ~Rs40,000cr (~US$5bn) GMV in 2026; share roughly Blinkit 45-50%, Zepto 20-25%, Instamart 20-25% — the new default access rail into Tier 2/3. (Source: Digital in Asia; Product Growth)

passages.title: India finding — demand
passages.text: Demand is shifting from awareness-led to access-led, driven by Gen Z, rising incomes, and vernacular/omnichannel reach; beauty has become a daily self-care essential, not aspirational luxury. (Source: Outlook Business (RedSeer))

passages.title: India finding — demand
passages.text: 'Skinification' is reshaping hair care (~US$4bn market): buyers want actives (niacinamide, ceramides, peptides) in serums/tonics; specialist D2C brands outperform legacy FMCG. (Source: Entrepreneur India; Arise)

passages.text: ~US$50m (H1 2025 basis), +44.7% YoY — small base, fast growth

passages.text: CDSCO import registration (Form COS-1 -> COS-2 via SUGAM portal) — pre-clearance before any consignment; key friction and lead-time cost

passages.title: Corridor — momentum
passages.text: K-beauty is accelerating its India entry to offset SWANA-region volatility (Personal Care Insights, Apr 2026). 2026 launches: APR's Medicube (Nykaa + Tira), AmorePacific's Illiyoon (Nykaa exclusive), TirTir (Nykaa, Jun 2026), Tira's Hince (Jan) and Dr. Melaxin (Jul). India K-beauty ~INR 3,139cr (2025) forecast ~26% CAGR to ~INR 32,424cr by 2035 (Expert Market Research). AmorePacific is scaling India via platforms/imports, NOT local manufacturing — no India plant announced.

passages.title: Q-commerce assortment insight
passages.text: Conglomerate-owned K-brands (AmorePacific, LG H&H) have mature India supply chains and are deeply stocked on q-commerce; the viral indie/derma brands driving the K-beauty narrative (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, 'coming soon', or absent. The real Tier 2/3 whitespace is getting indie derma K-beauty onto the q-commerce rail, not the conglomerate brands already there.
